title: Residency, audit evidence & hosting trade-offs - discovery with Northshore Trust Co
summary: Initial discovery between Redwood AE/SE and Northshore Trust to map residency constraints, logging retention and evidence requirements for a regulated financial use-case. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private trade-offs, KMS/HSM needs, audit logs, and a potential 6-week pilot with benchmark and redaction tests.
topics: dedicated vs private TCO and SLAs
action_items: Maya Chen: share security pack + SOC2 attestation and region availability matrix by 2027-09-27
Diego Alvarez: proposal for POC infra footprint and sample benchmark plan by 2027-09-30
Priya Sharma (Northshore): provide sample traffic profile and top 10 PII shapes by 2027-09-29
next_steps: Redwood to send security artifacts and proposed pilot SOW
Schedule 1-hour pilot scoping with Northshore infra and app teams next week
Run a short log-redaction spike during pilot and capture audit evidence
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-09-23
- Time: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 58 mins
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Rina (Redwood CSM); Helen (Northshore Head of Data Governance), Owen (CISO), Priya (Platform Ops), Samir (Legal)

Summary: quick intake focused on what Northshore needs for their custodial/trust workloads. Primary constraints: EU customer residency for accounts domiciled in EEA; logs must be retained for 7 years for audit (financial regs), but must be redacted before leaving customer control, keys must be customer-managed and preferably in-country. They're evaluating three hosting models: Hosted (fast), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), Private (VPC / on-prem).

00:00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for making time, we wanted to map out the residency and audit needs up front so we can size the right path, hi Helen, Owen.
00:00:10 Helen Park: hi Maya, thanks. yeah, outline would be great, we have a pretty tight compliance bar so want to get into specifics.
00:00:18 Owen Reed: Before we go deep, quick callout: we're looking for a pattern that passes both our internal auditors and external reg exam requirements — evidence chain is key.
00:00:29 Diego Alvarez: totally, we've done a bunch of work with financials to package evidence. quick q for Owen — is key residency strictly required by jurisdiction or is it more of a policy preference?
00:00:39 Owen Reed: in our case, it's required for a subset of accounts — EU domiciled accts must have keys within the EU and we cannot copy audit logs out of region without redaction.
00:00:49 Priya Sharma: and operationally, we need to be able to revoke and rotate keys without Redwood having access.
00:00:55 Maya Chen: ok, good. so initial options: Hosted (fast onboarding, but we'd need region-locking and KMS support), Dedicated (you get reserved capacity in a region, easier to meet isolation needs), Private (VPC or on-prem gives max control but higher ops). are we aligned so far?
00:01:12 Helen Park: yes, and we need to understand what kind of evidence Redwood can provide — e.g., access logs, control plane audit trails, and how immutable those logs are. also chain-of-custody for keys.
00:01:25 Diego Alvarez: we can provide control plane audit trails and token-level call traces. typical hosted approach uses regional tenancy and KMS integration; we can show attestations for region restrictions. for dedicated and private, you can have a private control plane and bring your own KMS (BYOK) or HSM. caveat: on hosted we have shared control plane components historically, but we do region isolation for data-at-rest.
00:01:49 Samir Das: when you say BYOK, does Redwood hold any key material for recovery or escrow? legal needs to know if Redwood can access plaintext.
00:01:56 Diego Alvarez: by default, Redwood doesn't hold customer keys. we offer a KMS integration where you store keys in your KMS/HSM; we do surface an optional key-escrow for emergency recovery but that requires contract and separate escrow protections.
00:02:11 Owen Reed: would need that opt-in and contractually limited.
00:02:14 Maya Chen: noted. Helen, can you share the kinds of records your auditors ask for during an exam? is it a sample of API calls, configuration snapshots, or a full-year rolling audit?
00:02:26 Helen Park: it's both. for year one they'll usually ask for configuration drift and a sample of request/response logs for critical flows. also, we have to demonstrate redaction rules don't leak PII outside region.
00:02:38 Diego Alvarez: on redaction we have two patterns: agent-side redaction (you sanitize before sending) or server-side token scrubbing in the pipeline. server-side can be done in the same region if using dedicated/private. hosted model can support server-side redaction if we deploy redaction modules in the EU region and ensure logs exported are scrubbed prior to leaving region.
00:02:58 Priya Sharma: important question — what is the retention granularity? we can't keep full transcripts with PII for 7 years in plaintext. we need an append-only audit trail that stores hashes plus redacted snapshots. can Redwood produce signed digests?
00:03:12 Diego Alvarez: yes, we can produce cryptographic digests of events and store redacted artifacts. for dedicated/private we can store all artifacts in your S3 bucket or object store in-region; for hosted we can provide the digests and push to your archive in-region on cadence.
00:03:28 Owen Reed: network controls — we require that egress endpoints are only within the region, and we need proof of that for auditors. is switchable in your product?
00:03:36 Maya Chen: Yup, we have routing policies and can pin requests to region, and we can restrict cross-region fallback. tradeoff is higher cold-start and maybe higher cost.
00:03:44 Helen Park: we also need to know what gets into service logs — for example, KV cache keys and long-term caches, do those contain identifying info?
00:03:53 Diego Alvarez: quick note: we do a KV cache for performance; we recommend a hashing layer or tokenization for PII. we can configure prefix caching to avoid materializing raw PII. there's also an option to disable KV caching per route for the most sensitive flows.
00:04:11 Samir Das: any third-party sub processors? auditors will want a list.
00:04:16 Rina Patel: we can share the current subprocessor list — it's in the security pack — and we keep it updated.
00:04:23 Priya Sharma: latency and cost hit — if we go fully private we might be owning GPUs and ops. can you give a rough TCO delta between dedicated and private?
00:04:33 Maya Chen: ballpark: dedicated is typically 20–40% more than hosted per token but with reserved capacity and predictable throughput; private (on-prem) has higher upfront ops but lower marginal inference cost if you amortize GPUs across many models — depends on your utilization. we'll have Diego draft a POC estimate.
00:04:49 Diego Alvarez: also quantization and batching profiles matter — we can recommend a quantization profile that reduces memory footprint to lower infra cost while keeping latency SLOs.
00:04:58 Helen Park: for the pilot we want to exercise: region-locking, KMS rotation, log redaction, and one end-to-end audit package. timeline is tight — board wants preliminary evidence in 6 weeks.
00:05:10 Maya Chen: 6 weeks is doable for a focused pilot. proposal: week 1 — infra setup + BYOK connection; week 2 — run synthetic traffic and redaction tests; week 3–4 — ingest small subset of real traffic under consent and capture evidence; week 5 — compile audit package and run internal review; week 6 — deliver package.
00:05:25 Owen Reed: who owns the data during pilot? we want data to remain customer-owned and not used for model training.
00:05:30 Maya Chen: Redwood's standard language is we do not use customer data for model training unless explicitly contracted. we will include that in the SOW.
00:05:38 Priya Sharma: about logs: we want them to be stored in our cloud account, in a dedicated bucket in eu-west-1, with object lockdown and lifecycle rules to keep two forms: redacted snapshot + hashed index. can Redwood push logs to our bucket?
00:05:49 Diego Alvarez: yes, we support pushing to customer-owned S3/GCS buckets and can sign the artifacts. we can also mount your object store for private deployments.
00:05:58 Samir Das: regarding legal, we need to see contract language on key escrow and liability if keys are lost.
00:06:03 Maya Chen: we'll flag legal to route that. Samir, Redwood legal can do an exception matrix and escrow terms if needed.
00:06:10 Helen Park: one more: we have a subsidiary in Switzerland — some accounts have additional constraints like no US human access even for support. can you do a nested access policy?
00:06:20 Diego Alvarez: yes, RBAC can be configured to limit support access to specific regions and we can require support access be done via recorded bastion sessions; also can add MFA and request time-limited access tokens.
00:06:33 Priya Sharma: any automated evidence for who accessed logs? we need user-level trails.
00:06:38 Diego Alvarez: we provide token-level call tracing and a control plane audit trail with user, action, timestamp. for private deployments the control plane is customer-managed so you get native cloud IAM logs as well.
00:06:50 Helen Park: what about HIPAA overlap? some of our lines of business want both financial controls and HIPAA. is Redwood OK with PHI retention needs?
00:06:58 Maya Chen: we support HIPAA workflows — isolation + BYOK are typical. we can provide an addendum for HIPAA handling and BAAs.
00:07:06 Owen Reed: regarding retention length — you said earlier you can produce signed digests. auditors often want chain-of-custody proofs (who exported what when). can those be signed by our HSM?
00:07:16 Diego Alvarez: yes, if you provide an external signing key in your HSM we can use that to sign artifacts at export time. that's more of a private/dedicated feature but we can wire it for hosted with contract.
00:07:29 Helen Park: great. also, we need a statement on data minimization — we can't have unbounded logs of debug-level info. can you tune log verbosity?
00:07:36 Rina Patel: yes, Redwood Console lets you configure per-route logging levels and token-level cost/latency sampling. for the pilot we'll set those to minimal and keep request traces hashed.
00:07:47 Samir Das: any mention of regulatory carve outs — e.g., binding corporate rules?
00:07:51 Maya Chen: Redwood has standard SCCs and can discuss BCRs for enterprise. we'll surface legal artifacts.
00:07:58 Priya Sharma: what about model fingerprinting and model variants? we want to fall back to lighter models during peak but ensure same quality for audit flows. how do you manage rollouts?
00:08:08 Diego Alvarez: rollouts can be canary'd in Redwood Console. you can pin a subset of routes to a verified model variant and fallback policies are explicit; we can exclude audit-critical flows from automatic fallback.
00:08:20 Helen Park: okay, so concrete asks for pilot SOW: show region-locking proof, BYOK integration, log redaction verification, signed export digests, and control-plane audit trail.
00:08:31 Maya Chen: perfect, Diego will outline the infra and SOW. Rina will send the security pack.
00:08:36 Diego Alvarez: quick technical note — the redaction pattern: we recommend a staged pipeline: agent-side PII tokenization (client SDK), server-side scrub + redaction module in-region, then a signed export to your bucket with hash index. this minimizes risk.
00:08:53 Priya Sharma: client SDK changes are okay, but we need minimal engineering lift. what's typical integration time?
00:08:59 Maya Chen: for a small set of routes it's often 2–4 engineers-days for tokenization + test harness. we'll scope it.
notes: Call ended with agreement to create a 6-week pilot SOW; Redwood to provide security pack and POC estimate. Customer to provide sample traffic and PII patterns. Legal to review key escrow terms if needed.
